judgment.rationale: Same-grain Indicator pair (C217, C220), both resolved to Class X (rank 1) within Chapter 14 'Sources of Energy' under the Natural Resources content domain, but with distinct parent CDSLOs (CLO95 differentiating forms of energy; CLO96 planning investigations on energy sources). C217 requires learners to compare and contrast conventional versus non-conventional energy sources — i.e., to classify and evaluate source types. C220 applies exactly that classificatory understanding in an extended investigative task: profiling a city/state/country's electricity mix across thermal, hydel, nuclear and 'other alternatives'. Command of the conventional/non-conventional distinction substantively supports success in interpreting and categorising the sources in a real energy profile, and the second statement adds investigation, data gathering and contextual application beyond simple comparison, so the same-rank developmental direction runs first to second rather than the reverse. Shared chapter, page 82 proximity and the 'energy'/'sources' token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient; the judgment rests on the pair-specific skill relationship. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each), so the visible excerpts may not represent the full source record.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain, same resolved coordinate (Class X, rank 1), in Chapter 7 'Control and Coordination' under 'The World of the Living'. CLO33 asks learners to explain the processes/phenomena/mechanisms of control and coordination in animals/plants, which includes the mechanism of hormonal regulation in plants; CLO37 requires applying that same learning about plant hormonal regulation to hypothetical situations and predicting consequences/implications. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators in the same grain (Chapter 1 'Matter in our surroundings', Content Domain 'Materials'), so the comparison is within-type and same-rank (Class IX, rank 0). Beyond shared wording and page, the statements differ substantively in demand: C58 (second) describes the structure of atoms and identifies the subatomic particles — electrons, protons, neutrons — and their arrangement (LCs 'Describes the structure of atoms', 'Identifies the subatomic particles ... and their arrangement'), which is the foundational descriptive knowledge of atomic constituents. C57 (first) explains the structure of the atom per Bohr's model and how that model overcomes the drawbacks of Rutherford's model (LCs on Bohr's model and its comparative advantage), requiring model-level explanation and evaluation that presupposes knowing the particles and their arrangement. Proficiency with C58 therefore supports success on C57, justifying same-rank direction second_to_first rather than symmetric relatesTo. C91 (second SFI) asks learners to relate tropic movements in plants to the stimulus that triggers them — identifying the stimulus–response correspondence. CLO105 has students plan and conduct investigations to become aware of the factors impacting the immediate and larger ecosystem (parent NCERT LO3, investigation/verification), producing first-hand knowledge of which environmental factors act on organisms. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (rank 0) in Chapter 8 - Motion under the 'Moving things, People and Ideas' Content Domain, so the same-grain and same-coordinate conditions hold and direction must rest on substantive evidence. C128 (first) is representational construction: 'Plots graphs from a given data or from personal experience (distance-time, speed-time, acceleration-time graphs)', with LCs for plotting distance-time, speed-time and acceleration-time graphs. C127 (second) is quantitative extraction and computation: 'Calculates the physical quantities related to motion (displacement, speed, velocity, acceleration) in a word problem and from a graph', with an explicit LC 'calculates ... from a graph'. Fluency in constructing and correctly scaling distance-time/speed-time/acceleration-time graphs materially supports reading slopes, intercepts and areas to compute displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration from a graph, so proficiency in C128 supports success in C127; the reverse (word-problem calculation) does not similarly require plotting. The two sit under different parent CLOs (CLO55 'Draws graphs...' vs CLO54 'Calculates the unknown variable...'), which supports a construction-to-application progression rather than mere duplication. Judgment is moderated because C127 also covers non-graph word problems, both endpoints' source evidence is truncated, and multiple ancestors carry upstream merge/code audit context (including a same_code_different_content flag on LO6) that was not resolved here.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain and same resolved coordinate (Class X, rank 1) under Chapter 8 'How Do Organisms Reproduce' in 'The World of the Living'. CLO50 (second) requires explaining the processes and phenomena of reproduction in plants and animals; CLO52 (first) requires analysing and interpreting data/graphs on contraception, STDs and sex determination. Beyond the shared chapter (which alone is not sufficient), the content is substantively dependent: contraception, STD transmission and sex determination are applications and consequences of the reproductive processes explained in CLO50, and the demand escalates from conceptual explanation (parent LO5, 'explains processes and phenomena') to data/graph analysis and interpretation (parent LO7, 'analyses and interprets data/graph/figure'). Proficiency in explaining reproduction therefore supports success in interpreting reproductive-health and sex-determination data, justifying a same-rank developmental direction from CLO50 to CLO52 rather than the reverse. Token/trigram and page-proximity signals are weak and were not treated as evidence of relation. Both endpoints carry merge/audit context and truncated source evidence, so only the supplied descriptions and source excerpts were used.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators at the same Class IX coordinate (rank 0) within Chapter 7 'Diversity in living organisms', so same-grain comparison is appropriate and direction must rest on substantive content. C105 requires learners to assign representative plant and animal specimens to their respective hierarchical subgroups using key characteristics; C107 requires relating evolutionary linkages between phyla/divisions/classes among plants and animals in terms of body design/characteristics. C107 presupposes command of the very taxonomic subgroups and characteristic-based criteria that C105 establishes, and moves from placement within a hierarchy to reasoning about evolutionary relationships between those groups — a substantive extension rather than mere repetition. Proficiency in C105 therefore supports success in C107. Note that shared Chapter/Content Domain ancestry, LC tag overlap ('plants', 'animals', 'classification') and page-34 proximity were only nomination triggers; the judgment rests on the statement texts. Their differing NCERT LO parents (LO2 classification vs LO4 relating processes with causes/effects) are read as distinct DAG paths, not a contradiction. Source evidence for both SFIs is truncated (32 and 24 omitted items), so this is a bounded-evidence inference.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain and coordinate (Class X, rank 1) within the 'Light – Reflection and Refraction' chapter of the Natural Phenomena domain. CLO72 (first) is qualitative/conceptual: explaining the types of images formed by different mirrors and lenses and the role of medium/density in refraction. CLO74 (second) is quantitative: calculating focal length, centre of curvature, magnification and refractive index from given data, and it hangs under the calculation-oriented NCERT LO8 while CLO72 hangs under the explanation-oriented LO5. Proficiency in explaining how images form for specific mirror/lens types and how medium density governs refraction supplies the conceptual referents (object/image positions, curvature, bending in a denser medium) that the calculations of magnification, focal length and refractive index operate on, so same-rank forward support from the explanatory outcome to the computational outcome is substantively grounded rather than mere chapter or wording overlap (the reported token overlap is only stopwords). judgment.rationale: Both are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain, same Class X coordinate (rank 1) and same Chapter 'Light – Reflection and Refraction' under Natural Phenomena, so hierarchy alone is not decisive. Pair-specific content does support a direction: CLO70 (second UUID) asks learners to differentiate reflection from refraction — a foundational discrimination of the two phenomena — while CLO72 (first UUID) requires explaining the types of images formed by different mirrors and lenses and the role of medium/density in refraction, i.e. causal explanation of each phenomenon's behaviour and its dependence on medium. Securely distinguishing reflection from refraction supports success in explaining mirror/lens image formation and medium-dependent refraction, so CLO70 builds towards CLO72 (second_to_first). The parent NCERT outcomes are consistent with this (LO1 'differentiates...' for CLO70 vs LO5 'explains processes and phenomena' for CLO72), though parents are context only. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, so the judgment rests on the supplied statement texts.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators at the same grain and the same resolved coordinate (Class IX, rank 0) within Chapter 'The fundamental unit of life'. C65 ('Differentiates between the processes of osmosis and diffusion with relevant examples and situations') establishes the conceptual discrimination of the two transport processes, while C70 ('Relates the processes of osmosis and diffusion in daily lives and situations', e.g. wrinkled fingers after soap-solution exposure) requires transferring those already-distinguished processes to explain everyday phenomena. This is a pair-specific substantive shift from differentiating the two processes to causal application in lived contexts, reflected in the distinct parent CDSLOs (CLO24 differentiation-focused vs CLO26 relating processes to causes/effects) and the C70 learning components that name osmosis and diffusion separately in daily-life terms. Being able to tell osmosis from diffusion supports success in explaining which process accounts for a given daily-life situation, so a same-rank forward direction from C65 to C70 is supported beyond the shared chapter, wording and LC overlap, which alone would not suffice. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/code audit context, so the judgment rests on the supplied indicator texts, coordinates, and LCs.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (rank 0, same coordinate) in Chapter 7 'Diversity in living organisms' under the World of the Living domain, but they sit under different parents and express different grains of the same classification strand. C108 states the conceptual basis of kingdom-based classification and the key characteristics of Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia; C113 requires drawing flow charts that classify plants and animals into groups and subgroups based on their characteristics (parent CLO46 under LO7, the diagram/flow-chart representation outcome). Knowing the basis of classification and each kingdom's distinguishing characteristics is the substantive content that a learner must apply to construct a hierarchical flow chart of plant and animal groups and subgroups, so proficiency in C108 supports success in C113 even though ranks are equal; the direction is grounded in this content-to-representation dependency, not merely shared chapter or the 'characteristics/classification' token overlap. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 32 omitted items) and all involved SFIs carry upstream merge/code audit context, so this judgment rests on the bounded descriptions, LCs, and hierarchy supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same resolved coordinate (Class IX, rank 0) within Chapter 7 'Diversity in living organisms'. CLO40 (second) requires differentiating major groups/subgroups of plants and animals (angiosperm, gymnosperm, pteridophyte, Arthropoda, Nematoda) on salient features/body design; CLO41 (first) requires placing plants and animals into various hierarchical subgroups on major characteristics. The substantive same-rank evidence for direction is that feature-based discrimination of groups is the enabling skill for assigning organisms into an ordered hierarchy of subgroups, and this is corroborated by the distinct trustworthy parent paths in the DAG: CLO40 sits under NCERT LO1 ('Differentiates ... based on properties/characteristics') while CLO41 sits under LO2 ('Classifies ... under various hierarchical sub-groups'), i.e., differentiation supporting classification rather than mere repetition of shared Chapter/Content Domain wording. Shared ancestors, page 34 proximity and token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (32 and 24 omitted items) and both carry upstream merge/code audit context, which limits certainty but does not conflict with the stated descriptions.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain, same Class IX coordinate (rank 0), within Chapter 13 'Why do we fall ill?' under 'World of living'. CLO94 requires describing the spread, causes, prevention and treatment of diseases; CLO97 requires applying knowledge of infectious agents, transmission, symptoms and treatment to design preventive strategies for community containment. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain, same resolved coordinate (Class X, rank 1), under the same Chapter 9 'Heredity and Evolution' organizer within 'The World of the Living'. CLO58 (second) is the investigative-practice outcome: 'Plans and conducts investigation/experiment around inherited traits, evolution and sex-determination' (parent NCERT LO3, planning/conducting investigations). CLO64 (first) is the inference outcome on the same content: 'Draws conclusions, such as traits/features are inherited through genes present on chromosomes, a new species originates through evolutionary processes' (parent NCERT LO14, drawing conclusions). The shared subject matter (inherited traits, evolution) with a shift from designing and carrying out investigations to deriving warranted conclusions is a substantive, pair-specific change in cognitive demand within the same inquiry cycle, so proficiency in planning/conducting these heredity and evolution investigations supports success in drawing the corresponding conclusions. Direction is same-rank but justified by this evidence rather than by shared chapter, token overlap, or page proximity alone. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain, Class IX (rank 0), Chapter 13 'Why do we fall ill?' under 'The World of the Living'. CLO87 establishes classification of diseases as acute/chronic and infectious/non-infectious together with their causes, types, treatment, transmission and prevention (parent LO1, differentiation). CLO91 narrows to a causal-relational skill (parent LO4, relating processes to causes/effects): matching the kind of treatment to the type of pathogen. Chapter/domain sharing, page proximity and the 'treatment/of' token overlap were treated as nomination signals only. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (same coordinate rank 0) in Chapter 2 'Is matter around us pure?' under Content Domain 'Materials', so the judgment rests on statement content rather than shared organizers. C19 has learners investigate the types and properties of mixtures, solutions, colloids and suspensions through simple experiments (LCs decompose this into mixtures, solutions, colloids, suspensions). C27 requires explaining the method of separating components of a specific heterogeneous mixture (sand, common salt, ammonium chloride/camphor), i.e. selecting and justifying sublimation/dissolution-filtration-evaporation steps that depend on the differing properties of the components. Knowing what type of mixture is present and how its components' properties differ is the substantive basis for explaining an appropriate separation sequence, and the parent CDSLOs mirror this (CLO7 investigating nature/properties of substances; CLO8 describing separation methods). This is a same-rank content-grounded developmental direction from characterising mixtures to explaining separation of a mixture's components, not mere wording or row proximity (token/trigram overlap is only stopword-level). Confidence is moderate because both indicators sit in one class and source evidence for each endpoint is truncated.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements at the same resolved coordinate (Class IX, rank 0) within Chapter 7 'Diversity in living organisms' under the 'World of living' Content Domain, so the same-grain and same-class conditions hold and direction must rest on substantive evidence, not shared parentage. C105 (under CLO41/LO2, 'Classifies plants and animals under various hierarchical subgroups based on major characteristics') requires applying key characteristics to assign representative specimens to hierarchical subgroups. C116 (under CLO49/LO14, 'Draws conclusion by drawing connections between larger principles of classification and the process of evolution') requires concluding an organism's place in a subgroup using classification principles plus its morphological and physiological development over time. The second task presupposes and extends the first: the same representative-specimen/subgroup assignment skill is reused but at higher cognitive demand (assign by observable characteristics → reason and conclude placement using classification principles integrated with evolutionary development), so proficiency in C105 supports success in C116. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Indicators (rank 1) in Chapter 7 'Control and Coordination' under 'The World of the Living', but they sit on different parent CDSLOs in the DAG: C92 under CLO31 (relating hormones to their functions) and C108 under CLO42 (values/objectivity in debating hormonal and nervous system disorders). C92 requires learners to relate observed symptoms of hormonal disorders to specific hormonal deficiencies in animals; C108 requires applying objectivity and myth-free rational thinking when debating hormonal and nervous-system disorder claims (e.g. that dwarfism/gigantism are not hereditary, or that late menarche implies infertility). The causal symptom-to-deficiency understanding in C92 is the substantive content base that makes the myth-refuting, evidence-based reasoning in C108 achievable, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. This is a content-to-application deepening within the same Indicator grain, not mere shared chapter/LC wording (token overlap is low, jaccard ~0.10, shared tokens limited to 'disorders'/'hormonal'). Direction is asserted despite equal Class rank on this pair-specific dependency; both endpoints carry merge/audit context and truncated source evidence, which limits but does not contradict the reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (rank 0) in Chapter 8 – Motion under 'Moving things, People and Ideas'. C120 (second) asks learners to differentiate uniform vs non-uniform motion and velocity vs acceleration using examples and graphs; C127 (first) asks learners to calculate displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration in word problems and from graphs. The qualitative discrimination of these kinematic quantities and their graphical signatures (C120's LCs: 'differentiates between velocity and acceleration using examples and graphs', 'uniform and non-uniform motion using examples and graphs') is the conceptual grounding that supports the quantitative graph- and word-problem computation demanded by C127 (LCs on calculation from a graph and in a word problem), which sits under the calculation-oriented CLO54/LO6 branch while C120 sits under the differentiation-oriented CLO51/LO1 branch. This is a substantive increase in demand from identifying/distinguishing quantities to computing them, so same-rank direction from C120 to C127 is justified rather than mere shared-chapter or token overlap. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and several ancestors carry merge/code audit context, so the judgment rests on the visible statement text and LCs.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators of the same grain at the same resolved coordinate (Class IX, rank 0) under CLO24 'Differentiates organisms... plant and animal cells'. C67 (first) requires identifying major cell organelles - explicitly including chloroplast, cell membrane and cell wall - from temporary mounts, permanent slides and pictures; its LC confirms observational identification of these structures. C63 (second) requires recognising that cell walls and chloroplasts differentiate plant cells from animal cells, with LCs on chloroplast and cell wall as discriminating features. Same-rank direction is supported by substantive content difference: proficiency in locating/identifying the cell wall and chloroplast in observed material supports success in then using exactly those two structures as criteria to classify plant versus animal cells, which is a comparative/inferential step beyond identification. Shared Chapter, Content Domain, page 29 proximity and 'cell/wall' token overlap were treated as nomination signals only, not as the basis of the judgment. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source evidence items each), and organizer ancestors carry merge audit context, so the excerpted indicator text and single shared parent are the trustworthy basis here.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements in the same Class IX / Materials / 'Structure of atoms' chapter under CLO22 ('Traces the journey of the structure of an atom from the Thomson to the Bohr model'), so the same-type grain and shared DAG parentage are satisfied. C53 (second) asks learners to describe the structure of the atom as per Rutherford's atomic model; C56 (first) asks learners to state the drawbacks of that same model. Knowing what the Rutherford model asserts about atomic structure is the substantive content on which any critique of its limitations (e.g., instability of orbiting electrons) rests, so proficiency with C53 supports success with C56. This is a pair-specific content dependency, not mere shared wording, chapter, LC tags, or page proximity; both sit at the same Class IX rank (0), and the direction is justified by the descriptive-to-evaluative content relationship rather than by code order or rank. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Indicators (rank 1, same-rank) in Chapter 3 'Metals and Non-metals' under Content Domain 'Materials', so same statement-type grain is satisfied and direction must rest on substantive content, not rank. C36 (second) asks learners to compare melting and boiling points of common everyday compounds (common salt, calcium carbonate, textbook table 3.5) — a concrete physical-property data comparison. C18 (first) asks learners to classify ionic and covalent compounds based on their physical properties. The supplied parent evidence makes the dependency explicit rather than merely lexical: C36's parents CLO11 ('Analyses data to differentiate between covalent and ionic compounds on the basis of melting point and boiling point') and LO7 ('melting and boiling points of substances to differentiate between covalent and ionic compounds') identify melting/boiling-point comparison as the evidentiary basis for the ionic/covalent distinction, while C18 sits under CLO7/LO2 classification outcomes. Facility with comparing melting/boiling points of specific compounds therefore supports success in the broader classification of ionic versus covalent compounds by physical properties, giving second_to_first. Shared ancestors, page proximity and thin token overlap ('and', 'compounds') were not treated as sufficient on their own. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (32 and 24 omitted items) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream merge/code context, so the reading rests on the bounded excerpts and parent texts provided.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators at the same grain and same resolved coordinate (Class X, rank 1) within Chapter 5 'Periodic classification of elements' under the 'Materials' Content Domain, so the judgment rests on pair-specific content rather than shared ancestry. C52 (first) requires classifying elements by the early classification schemes — Dobereiner's triads, Newlands' law of octaves and Mendeleev's periodic table (its LCs name exactly these three) — establishing the ideas of ordering elements by property repetition, groups and periods. C54 (second) requires explaining periodic properties (atomic size, valency, metallic character) as they vary across periods and down groups in the Modern Periodic Table, i.e. reasoning about periodicity and trends within the mature tabular arrangement; its own parent CLO16 concerns features of the modern periodic table and position-based reactivity, whereas C52's parent CLO15 is the more basic 'classifies elements based on specific properties'. Facility with the earlier classification attempts and the periodicity/group-period concept they introduce substantively supports success in explaining trends in the modern table, so the same-rank developmental direction is lower-complexity classification toward higher-complexity trend explanation, not mere shared wording ('elements', 'periodic table'). judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators of the same grain within Class X, Content Domain 'Natural Resources', Chapter 15 'Our Environment', so the statement-type grain and identity scope are compatible. C240 (second) asks learners to categorise organisms in terms of trophic levels, while C248 (first) asks them to relate biomagnification to increasing concentration of non-biodegradable substances along the food chain. Beyond shared wording, there is a pair-specific conceptual dependency: recognising and ordering trophic levels is the structural basis on which progressive accumulation of non-biodegradable substances up the food chain can be explained, so proficiency with C240 supports success with C248, not the reverse. Rank is equal (both Class X, rank 1), so the direction rests on this substantive conceptual layering (categorisation of the chain structure -> quantitative/causal reasoning about accumulation within it), corroborated by their placement in adjacent source table rows (95 then 97) under different parent CLOs (CLO104 differentiation vs CLO106 relating). Shared ancestors, LC token overlap ('food', 'chain') and page proximity alone were not treated as sufficient. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both SFIs is truncated (32 and 24 omitted items) and several ancestors carry merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded descriptions and LC claims supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements in Class IX (rank 0), sharing parent CLO34 'Relates type of tissues with functions and habitat of plant and animals' under Chapter 6 – Tissues, so grain and scope are comparable. C90 has learners relate features and characteristics of a bounded set (simple permanent tissues in plants) to their functions through direct observation of prepared slides; C92 extends the same structure-function reasoning outward to link tissue characteristics and functions to the habitat of both plants and animals. The pair-specific change is substantive rather than repetitive: broadened organism scope (plants to plants and animals), tissue scope (simple permanent to tissues generally), and an added ecological inference step that presupposes a secure structure-to-function mapping. Established proficiency in the observational structure-function relation (C90) therefore supports likely success in the function-to-habitat relation (C92); the reverse dependency is not supported by the evidence. Shared LC token overlap ('tissues', 'characteristics', 'functions', 'plants') and same-page provenance were treated as nomination signals only, not as the basis of the verdict. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all context nodes carry merge/audit context, so this is an inference from bounded evidence rather than a claim about the full source.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators at the same resolved coordinate (Class IX, rank 0) within Chapter 7 'Diversity in living organisms' under the World of the Living Content Domain, so same-grain comparison applies and direction must rest on substantive content. C108 asks learners to describe the basis of kingdom-based classification and elaborate the key characteristics of Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia — the descriptive criteria and diagnostic features of the classification scheme. C116 asks learners to conclude where a representative organism belongs in a subgroup 'based on classification principles' and to relate that to morphological/physiological development over time — an applied, inferential use of exactly those criteria extended to evolutionary reasoning. Command verbs and parent paths corroborate this direction without being relied on alone: C108 sits under CLO44/LO5 (explains diversity and the basis of hierarchical classification), while C116 sits under CLO49/LO14 (draws conclusions connecting classification principles to evolution). Command of the kingdom criteria and features in C108 therefore supports likelihood of success in the placement-and-inference task of C116; the reverse is not supported. Shared ancestry, adjacent source pages, and the single shared token 'classification' were treated as nomination signals only. Endpoint source evidence is truncated (24 and 32 omitted items), so the judgment rests on the bounded descriptions, codes, and LCs supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Class IX Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes in the same chapter ('Why do we fall ill?', The World of the Living), so the same-grain and same-rank comparison is legitimate, but shared chapter/domain alone is not the basis here. CLO94 ('Describes the spread, causes, prevention and treatment of diseases', under NCERT LO5 'explains processes and phenomena') establishes the conceptual disease knowledge — transmission routes, causative agents, preventive and curative measures — that CLO89 ('Plans and conducts investigations around [prevalence], means, source, prevention and treatment of a disease in a community', under NCERT LO3 'plans and conducts investigations') requires learners to operationalise in a community inquiry. The second outcome extends the same content into inquiry design and field application, so proficiency in describing disease spread/causes/prevention/treatment supports success in planning and conducting such an investigation; the reverse direction is weaker because investigation planning presupposes the descriptive knowledge. Judgment is same-rank (Class IX, rank 0) and rests on the substantive knowledge-to-inquiry extension rather than the weak token/trigram and page-proximity signals. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (32 and 24 omitted items) and both carry upstream merge/audit context, and the CLO89 description contains an apparent source typo ('revalance'), read as 'prevalence'.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators at the same resolved coordinate (Class X, rank 1), so grain matches and direction must rest on substantive content. C168 (second) requires explaining the role of medium/density in refraction textually and diagrammatically — a qualitative, mechanism-level account of why and how light bends between media (LCs: 'explains the role of medium/density in refraction textually', '...diagrammatically'). C180 (first) requires applying the law of refraction quantitatively to compute angle of incidence, angle of refraction and refractive index with glass slab and prism (LCs on calculating angle of refraction, angle of incidence, refractive index). The qualitative grasp of medium/optical density as the determinant of bending is the conceptual basis on which refractive-index and Snell's-law calculations are performed, so proficiency in C168 supports success in C180; the reverse (calculation supporting conceptual explanation) is the weaker reading. This is a qualitative-to-quantitative deepening within the shared Class X 'Natural Phenomena' domain, not mere shared-ancestor or 'refraction' token overlap (jaccard only 0.16 on SFI text, one shared LC tag). judgment.rationale: Both are Class X (rank 1) Indicators in Chapter 6 Life Processes, judged within the same Indicator grain. C60 has learners plan and conduct an investigation establishing that carbon dioxide is released during respiration in germinating seeds; C77 requires drawing conclusions from experiments that anaerobic respiration specifically yields CO2 and alcohol. The same-rank direction is supported by a pair-specific substantive change rather than mere wording overlap: C60 secures the experimental detection of CO2 as a respiratory product at the level of conducting/validating an investigation, while C77 extends that to the more differentiated anaerobic pathway with an additional product (alcohol) and to the higher-order act of drawing conclusions from experimental evidence (its parent CLO25 'draws conclusions after performing experiments related to photosynthesis and respiration' versus C60's parent CLO18 'plans and conducts investigations'). Proficiency in detecting and validating CO2 release therefore supports success in concluding anaerobic respiration's products. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain, same coordinate (Class X, rank 1), and the same Chapter 8 'How Do Organisms Reproduce' within 'The World of the Living', so the grain and scope constraints are satisfied. CLO47 (second) asks learners to relate observable physical and behavioural changes at puberty to underlying hormonal changes — a causal-explanatory outcome under NCERT LO4 ('Relates processes and phenomena with causes/effects'). CLO53 (first) asks learners to apply learning of reproductive processes to hypothetical situations and predict consequences/implications — under NCERT LO11 ('Applies learning to hypothetical situations'). The pair-specific change is substantive rather than generic repetition: the same reproductive-process content is carried from establishing cause–effect relationships to using those relationships generatively to predict outcomes in novel, unobserved scenarios. Secure grasp of the hormonal causation behind pubertal change is a plausible support for successfully reasoning about hypothetical reproductive-process consequences, so the same-rank developmental direction runs from CLO47 to CLO53 (second_to_first in the technical canonical order). Distinct NCERT LO parents are read as parallel DAG paths, not a single sequence; shared chapter/domain and the weak token/trigram and page-proximity signals alone were not treated as sufficient. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 32 omitted items) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the visible outcome statements and may be revised against fuller evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements at the same resolved coordinate (Class IX, rank 0) within Chapter 15 'Improvement in food resources' (Content Domain: Food), so the statement-type grain and scope match, though shared ancestry alone is not decisive. Substantively, C257 requires the learner to relate modern crop and animal husbandry practices to greater yield/production and increased farmer income (a causal, cause-effect understanding under LO4/CLO111). C267 requires discussing the positions people adopt on the benefits and risks of intensive versus organic farming (an evaluative, socio-scientific argumentation task under LO5/CLO112, which frames best practices against environmental factors). Command of the productivity/income benefits established in C257 supplies the substantive 'benefit' side of the trade-off that C267 asks learners to weigh and debate, so proficiency in C257 plausibly supports success in C267; the reverse is not supported, since discussing stakeholder positions does not establish the causal practice-to-yield relation. Direction is same-rank but justified by the shift from causal explanation to evaluation of risks/benefits, not by rank or page proximity. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both SFIs is truncated (32 and 24 omitted items) and both endpoints and their ancestors carry upstream merge/code audit context, so the full source wording could refine this judgment.

CLO35 requires explaining the types of plant tissues (meristematic, permanent) and animal tissues (epithelial, connective, muscular, nervous); CLO38 requires creating 3-d models of those different types of animal and plant tissues using eco-friendly resources. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators at the same Class IX coordinate (rank 0) within Chapter 13 'Why do we fall ill?' of The World of the Living, so grain and topic match. C210 (second) 'Distinguishes between infectious and non-infectious diseases with suitable examples' sits under CLO87/LO1 (differentiation by characteristics) and establishes the basic two-category classification of disease with exemplars. C219 (first) 'Describes infectious and non-infectious diseases, their causes and manifestation' sits under CLO94/LO5 (explains spread, causes, prevention, treatment) and extends the same categories to causal agents and clinical manifestation across ten named diseases (coronary heart disease, asthma, cancer, malaria, polio, measles, cholera, AIDS, gonorrhoea, common cold), evidenced by its three LCs on classification, causes, and manifestation. Secure categorisation of infectious vs non-infectious disease with examples substantively supports success in explaining the causes and manifestations of specific diseases within those categories, so the developmental direction runs second_to_first rather than the reverse; the shared chapter and LC token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient. Direction at equal rank rests on this differentiate-then-explain parentage contrast, which is suggestive rather than conclusive, hence moderate confidence. CLO64 is the conclusion-drawing outcome that traits/features are inherited through genes present on chromosomes (and that new species originate through evolutionary processes); CLO62 requires applying that heredity/inheritance learning to predict trait expressions in a given situation. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain and coordinate (Class X, rank 1) within the same Chapter 'Sources of Energy' under Content Domain 'Natural Resources', so hierarchy alone is not decisive; the judgment rests on statement content. CLO97 (second) requires explaining processes/phenomena and factors relating to the various forms of energy available to the world — a conceptual/explanatory grasp of energy sources and their characteristics. CLO100 (first) requires applying that learning of energy sources and their major types to predict consequences of a hypothetical scenario (exhaustion of all non-renewable sources), which explicitly presupposes knowledge of energy sources and their types and raises cognitive demand from explanation to application/prediction. This pair-specific escalation supports a same-rank developmental direction from CLO97 to CLO100. Parent NCERT LOs corroborate the shift (LO5 'Explains processes and phenomena' vs LO11 'Applies learning to hypothetical situations... if all non-renewable sources of energy are exhausted'). Both endpoints carry upstream merge/audit context and truncated source evidence (32 omitted evidence items each), so the evidence base is bounded, but the retained statement text is unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements at the same Class X coordinate (rank 1) within Chapter 15 – Our Environment under the Natural Resources Content Domain, so the same-grain comparison is valid. C249 requires explaining food chains and webs in terms of interdependence and trophic levels (conceptual structure of energy transfer); C258 requires calculating the amount of energy available at various trophic levels in a food chain from given data. Understanding what trophic levels are and how energy/matter flows through a food chain is the conceptual basis that supports success in quantitatively computing energy at each level (e.g., applying the 10% flow idea). This is substantive extension from qualitative explanation to quantitative application, not mere wording overlap, so a same-rank developmental direction from C249 to C258 is supported. The differing parent Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes (CLO107 conservation/explanation vs CLO110 energy calculation) and NCERT LOs (LO5 explains vs LO8 calculates) corroborate the explain-then-calculate progression rather than contradicting it. Shared chapter, page proximity and LC token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and several ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, but the visible statement texts are unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes (same statement-type grain) under the same Chapter 'Light – Reflection and Refraction' within Content Domain 'Natural Phenomena', so the comparison is within-grain and within-topic. CLO73 ('Draws ray diagrams of different kinds of lenses.') is a representational construction skill; CLO72 ('Explains processes and phenomena, such as the type of images formed for different mirrors and lenses, the role of medium/density in refraction.') requires explanatory reasoning about image formation and refraction for the same optical elements. Facility with constructing lens ray diagrams supplies the representation learners use to reason about and justify image type, position and nature, so proficiency in CLO73 plausibly supports success in CLO72; the ranks are identical (Class X, rank 1), but the substantive shift from drawing a representation to explaining the phenomena it depicts supports this direction rather than a symmetric reading. The pair's different NCERT LO parents (LO6 diagram-drawing vs LO5 explaining processes) corroborate the representation-to-explanation shift rather than mere wording overlap ('different', 'lenses'). Source evidence for both SFIs is truncated and both endpoints and their ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded descriptions and hierarchy shown.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements in the same Class X coordinate (rank 1) within Chapter 3 'Metals and Non-metals' under Content Domain 'Materials', so the comparison is within one statement-type grain. C30 (second) is the empirical step: 'Infers the reactivity of the metals and arranges them in the decreasing order of reactivity based on the above results', with LCs 'infers the reactivity of metals based on experimental results' and 'arranges metals in decreasing order of reactivity based on experimental results'. C20 (first) is the more abstract explanatory step: 'Relates reactivity of metals to their position in the Periodic Table and their properties', with LCs tying reactivity to periodic-table position and to properties. Establishing and ordering a reactivity series from experimental evidence supplies the reactivity ordering that the periodic-position/property explanation operates on, so proficiency with C30 supports success with C20; the same-rank direction rests on this substantive empirical-to-explanatory shift rather than on shared chapter, shared LC tokens ('metals', 'reactivity'), or adjacent source pages, which alone would not establish a relation. Endpoints sit under different parent CLOs (CLO9 vs CLO7) in the DAG, which is compatible with complementary rather than hierarchical linkage. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (32 and 24 omitted items) and all cited SFIs carry upstream merge/code audit context, so the directional judgment is drawn from bounded evidence only.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain SFIs in Class IX (rank 0), Chapter 6 – Tissues, World of the Living, so the statement-type grain matches. C83 (second) asks learners to distinguish epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous animal tissues — identifying and differentiating the four animal tissue categories. C89 (first) goes substantively further within the same content: it requires relating the features and characteristics of one of those categories (connective tissue) to its functions in animals, and adds the practical demand of observing prepared slides. Being able to recognise and separate connective tissue from the other three animal tissue types plausibly supports success in analysing connective-tissue structure–function relationships microscopically, so a same-rank developmental direction from C83 to C89 is supported by the specific change in cognitive demand (differentiate → relate structure to function with slide observation), not merely by shared chapter, class, or the single shared LC token 'connective'. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Indicators (same statement-type grain, coordinate rank 1) under Chapter 8 'How Do Organisms Reproduce' in the Content Domain 'The World of the Living'. C128 (second) asks learners to explain methods of vegetative propagation with examples — concrete explanatory knowledge of an asexual reproductive process in plants (LC tags: asexual, plants, reproduction, vegetative propagation). C137 (first) asks learners to apply learning of reproductive processes to hypothetical situations and predict consequences/implications (LC tags: application, consequences, prediction, reproduction), e.g. unfertilised eggs or loss of pollinators. Within the same rank, the substantive change is a cognitive-demand escalation from explaining specific reproductive mechanisms to transferring that reproductive-process knowledge to novel hypothetical scenarios and predicting outcomes; secure explanatory command of plant reproductive methods supports success in that predictive application. Support is partial rather than exhaustive (C137's cited examples are human fertilisation and pollination rather than vegetative propagation), which is reflected in the moderate confidence; shared chapter/domain and weak lexical/page proximity signals alone were not treated as sufficient. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so this judgment rests on the bounded, non-fallback statement text and hierarchy shown.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes (CLO19, CLO21) at the same Class X coordinate (rank 1, gap 0) within Chapter 'Life Processes' / 'The World of the Living'. CLO19 asks learners to relate features of structures/organs in living beings to their functions; CLO21 asks them to explain the named life processes (photosynthesis, respiration, transpiration/translocation, digestion, transportation, excretion) together with the role of the associated structures/organs in plants and animals. Proficiency in linking organ features to functions therefore supports success in explaining the processes and the organs' roles, justifying a same-rank first_to_second direction rather than a merely symmetric link. CLO41 (second) requires classifying plants and animals into hierarchical subgroups based on major characteristics; CLO43 (first) requires relating evolutionary linkages between phyla/divisions/classes among plants and animals in terms of body design/characteristics. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements in the same grain, same Class IX coordinate (rank 0), same Content Domain 'The World of the Living' and Chapter 7 'Diversity in living organisms', so the comparison is within one coherent instructional unit. C112 requires drawing labelled diagrams of representative organisms and their identifying features/characteristics from various sub-groups — i.e., securing accurate knowledge and representation of the diagnostic features that underpin classification. Same-rank direction is grounded in this substantive cognitive-demand escalation, not in local rank, page proximity, or code order. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain NCERT Learning Outcomes (LO5 and LO11) under the same Class IX grouping at identical canonical rank 0, so direction rests on substantive content evidence rather than coordinate gap. LO5 requires explaining processes and phenomena including the effect of force on the state of motion of objects and the revolution of planets and satellites; LO11 requires applying that learning to hypothetical situations such as the weight of an object on the moon, weight at equator versus poles, and life on other planets. The LO11 exemplars are transfer applications of exactly the force/gravitation and planetary-motion phenomena LO5 asks students to explain, so explanatory proficiency in LO5 plausibly supports success in the novel-situation application demanded by LO11 (a substantive extension, not mere repeated wording; the shared tokens alone — 'and', 'such', 'planets', 'etc' — would not suffice). judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at Class X (rank 1) under Chapter 5 – Periodic classification of elements within the 'Materials' content domain, so direction must rest on substantive content, not rank. CLO15 ('Classifies elements based on specific properties', under NCERT LO2 classification) is the more elementary chemical-classification skill: sorting elements by characteristic properties. CLO16 ('Explains the features of modern periodic table and reactivity of elements based on their position in periodic table', under NCERT LO5 explanation of processes/phenomena including placement of elements in the modern periodic table) requires that classification ability and extends it to explanatory reasoning about the table's structural features and position-dependent reactivity trends. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements in the same Class X coordinate (rank 1) and the same Chapter 7 'Control and Coordination' under 'The World of the Living', so the grain and scope match. C86 (second) asks learners to classify plant movements as growth or non-growth movements — establishing the category system in which tropic (growth) movements sit. C95 (first) requires explaining tropic movements with reference to hormonal (auxin) regulation, i.e. accounting for the mechanism behind one of those categories. Command-verb and content evidence give a same-rank developmental direction: distinguishing and classifying the movement types supports success in explaining the hormonal mechanism of the tropic subtype, so C86 buildsTowards C95. Their differing CLO parents (CLO29 'Classifies...' vs CLO33 'Explains...' processes/mechanisms of control and coordination) corroborate the classify-then-explain progression rather than mere shared-parent proximity. Evidence limitation: both endpoints carry upstream merge/audit context and truncated source evidence (32 omitted items each), so only the bounded excerpts were used.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Indicators (rank 1) under Chapter 6 – Life Processes / The World of the Living, so same-grain comparison is appropriate. C59 (second) has students plan and conduct investigations validating gaseous exchange in plants/animals during photosynthesis/respiration and starch production, i.e. the experimental-design and data-gathering stage, with LCs tagged 'investigation', 'gaseous exchange', 'respiration'. C78 (first) requires drawing conclusions from experiments/activities that aerobic respiration results in CO2 and water — an inferential outcome about the specific products of respiration that rests on exactly the kind of gaseous-exchange investigation specified in C59. The substantive change is from conducting/validating gas-exchange investigations to inferring and concluding the chemical products of aerobic respiration, so proficiency with C59 supports success on C78; the shared respiration content and its parent CLO18 (plans/conducts investigations) versus CLO25 (draws conclusions from photosynthesis/respiration experiments) reinforce this inquiry-cycle direction rather than mere wording overlap. Direction is asserted on this pair-specific inquiry-stage evidence, not on equal Class X rank, shared chapter, or page proximity; endpoint merge/audit context and truncated source evidence limit certainty, hence moderate confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Indicators (rank 1) under the same CDSLO CLO59 ('Explains process/phenomenon/principles related to heredity and evolution') in Chapter 9 Heredity and Evolution, so the same-grain comparison is legitimate. C150 ('Discusses nature of evolution in terms of variation'; LC tags evolution, heredity, variation) establishes variation as the mechanism driving evolutionary change, while C149 ('Explains process of speciation'; LC tags evolution, heredity, speciation) requires applying that mechanism plus isolation/accumulated variation to explain how new species arise. Grasping evolution in terms of variation substantively supports success in explaining speciation, giving same-rank developmental support beyond mere shared parent, chapter, page-72 proximity, or generic token overlap ('of', 'ion'), which alone would not justify a relation. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and several ancestors carry merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the visible indicator texts and LC claims.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain SFIs at the same resolved coordinate (Class IX, rank 0) within the same Chapter 'Diversity in living organisms' of the Content Domain 'World of living', so the same-rank direction rests on statement content, not hierarchy or proximity. C113 (first) asks learners to draw flow charts that classify plants and animals into groups and subgroups based on their characteristics (LC tags: classification, characteristics, flow chart), i.e. constructing and representing the classification hierarchy itself. C116 (second), under CLO49/LO14 on drawing conclusions linking classification principles to evolution, asks learners to conclude the place of a representative organism in a subgroup using classification principles plus its morphological and physiological development over time (LC tags: classification, evolution, organism, subgroup). C116 presupposes command of group/subgroup classification criteria and adds inferential reasoning and an evolutionary/developmental dimension, so proficiency in C113 substantively supports success in C116; the reverse is not supported. Judgment is limited to the bounded excerpts: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (32 omitted items each) and all cited ancestors and endpoints carry upstream merge/audit context, though both coordinates resolved without fallback.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Indicators (same statement-type grain, resolved coordinate rank 1 for each) in the Natural Phenomena content domain. C168 (Chapter 10, Light – Reflection and Refraction, under CLO72 'role of medium/density in refraction') requires explaining refraction and its dependence on medium/density both textually and diagrammatically; its learning components explicitly cover the diagrammatic representation of refraction. C177 (Chapter 11, Human eye and colourful world, under CLO78 'Draws labelled diagrams for various concepts of light') requires drawing a labelled ray diagram of dispersion of white light through a prism, which is a refraction-based phenomenon depicted through bending at medium boundaries. Facility with explaining/representing refraction at a medium interface substantively supports success in constructing the labelled prism-dispersion diagram, so the same-rank direction second_to_first is supported by the conceptual dependency and the Chapter 10 → Chapter 11 light sequence, not merely by shared ancestors, the single shared LC tag 'diagram', or low token/trigram overlap (jaccard ~0.05–0.07). Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (32 omitted items each) and all cited SFIs carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded descriptions, codes, and hierarchy shown.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements at the same resolved coordinate (Class IX, rank 0) within Content Domain 'Food', Chapter 15 'Improvement in food resources', so the same-grain and same-scope conditions hold. C250 ('Distinguishes between micro and macro nutrients', under CLO107 on nutrient management, LO1 differentiation) establishes the classification of plant nutrients; C255 ('Relates crop productivity with usage of fertilisers', under CLO109, LO4 cause/effect relating) applies that nutrient knowledge to a causal relationship between fertiliser application and yield. Since fertilisers are the delivery of exactly those macro/micro nutrients, proficiency in distinguishing nutrient types substantively supports success in reasoning about how fertiliser usage affects crop productivity, which justifies a same-rank developmental direction from the classification indicator to the causal-application indicator rather than mere shared-chapter co-location (LC token overlap is only 'food' and trigram overlap is negligible, so those signals alone were not treated as sufficient). Ancestry was read as a DAG (Chapter/Content Domain path plus NCERT LO path) without flattening; all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated, so the judgment rests on the untruncated indicator statement texts and resolved coordinates.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes at the same grain and coordinate (Class X, rank 1) within Chapter 6 – Life Processes / The World of the Living. CLO17 asks learners to differentiate processes/phenomena/characteristics relating to life in plants and animals, while CLO21 asks them to explain those same life processes together with the role of the associated structures/organs (photosynthesis, respiration, transpiration, translocation; digestion, transportation, excretion). Within one class, distinguishing and classifying the life processes is the narrower discriminative skill that supports the broader explanatory task of accounting for mechanism and organ function, so proficiency in CLO17 plausibly supports success in CLO21; this pair-specific content deepening (identify/contrast → explain process and structure) is more than shared chapter, wording, or page proximity. The differing NCERT LO parents (LO1 'differentiates' vs LO5 'explains') corroborate the demand shift rather than contradicting it. Source evidence for both SFIs is truncated (24 omitted items each) and several ancestors carry merge context, which caps confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes in Class IX (rank 0) under Chapter 8 – Motion within 'Moving things, People and Ideas'. CLO51 (second, 'Differentiates between kinds of motion') establishes the qualitative conceptual distinctions of motion (chapter key concepts include uniform and non-uniform motion, distance/displacement, velocity), which is the conceptual basis for CLO56 (first, 'Analyses and interprets data, graphs related to motion'), a quantitative analysis/interpretation outcome aligned to NCERT LO8 on distance-time and velocity-time graphs and computing distance/speed/acceleration. Same-rank direction is supported by this substantive shift from differentiating motion types (parented to LO1, differentiation of phenomena) to graph/data analysis of the same motion quantities, so proficiency in CLO51 supports success in CLO56; shared chapter/domain and the single shared token 'motion' alone were not treated as sufficient. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, which limits but does not contradict this reading; the DAG parents (Chapter organizer plus distinct NCERT LO parents) were read separately rather than flattened.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (same grain, rank 0) under the same CLO24 parent in Chapter 5 'The fundamental unit of life'. C67 (first) requires identifying major cell organelles (nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, vacuoles, chloroplast, cell membrane, cell wall) from mounts/slides/pictures, while C66 (second) requires describing the differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells and organisms. The prokaryote/eukaryote contrast is defined precisely by the presence or absence of a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, so reliable recognition and naming of those organelles substantively supports success in articulating the structural contrast; the second statement is the more integrative, explanatory step over the identification skill. Same-rank direction is therefore grounded in the specific structure-to-comparison content relationship rather than shared parentage, page proximity, or the trivial 'and' token overlap noted in the nomination evidence. Endpoint source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and several ancestors carry merge/audit context, so this remains an inferred curriculum-grounded judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are Class IX Indicators (same rank 0) under the same parent CLO83 ('...verify the process of sound production and propagation, echo production, reflection of sound') in Chapter 12 – Sound, so shared placement alone is not decisive. The pair-specific evidence is substantive, however: C189 (second) has students experimentally verify that sound propagates differently through air, water and solids, while C191 (first) has them verify the conditions required to produce an echo. Echo conditions (a reflecting surface, sufficient distance relative to the speed of sound in the medium) presuppose that sound travels through and at a finite speed in a medium; the parent CLO also orders propagation before echo production. Experimental verification of medium-dependent propagation therefore supports success with the more complex echo-condition investigation, giving a second_to_first developmental direction rather than mere symmetric reinforcement. CLO7 establishes the conceptual classification of metals/non-metals by chemical properties and the relation of ionic, covalent and metallic bonding to physical and chemical properties. CLO11 requires analysing empirical data (melting and boiling points, colour change in metal salt solutions) to differentiate covalent from ionic compounds and metals from non-metals, and to relate observations to reactivity. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX Indicators (rank 0) under the same Chapter 'Tissues' organizer, but they differ substantively in demand. C84 (second) is an observational identification skill: 'Identifies striped, smooth and cardiac muscle fibres and nerve cells in animals using prepared/permanent slides', with LCs each scoped to recognizing one tissue type on slides. C93 (first) requires explanation of structure AND function across a broader set of animal tissues (the same muscle fibre types and nerve cells, plus connective tissues — bone, cartilage, tendon — and epithelial tissue), with LCs at the 'explains structure and functions' level. Reliable slide-based identification of striated, smooth and cardiac muscle fibres and nerve cells plausibly supports success in explaining their structure and functions, and C93 extends the same content to additional tissue categories; hence a same-rank developmental direction from C84 to C93 rather than mere symmetric reinforcement. Shared ancestry, page proximity, and token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient; the decision rests on the pair-specific shift from identification to explanation plus broadened tissue coverage. Note the two endpoints sit under different parent CLOs (CLO31 differentiation vs CLO35 explanation) in the DAG and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated, which limits certainty somewhat.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X Indicators (same grain, same rank 1) in Chapter 15 – Our Environment under the Natural Resources content domain, but they sit under different Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes (C247 under CLO105 'plans and conducts investigations ... factors impacting the ecosystem'; C260 under CLO112 'makes efforts and takes steps to conserve environment ... segregation ... recycling and reusage'). C247 is an inquiry outcome: investigating the ways of recycling waste products and their environmental impact (LCs: 'investigates the ways of recycling waste products', 'investigates the impact of recycling waste products on the environment'). C260 is an applied/dispositional outcome: taking conservation action and promoting segregation of biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes with appropriate recycling and reuse, grounded in biotic/abiotic interdependence. The overlap is not merely wording ('recycling', 'waste', 'environment'): understanding which recycling routes exist and what environmental impact they have substantively supports informed, purposeful promotion of segregation, recycling and reuse, so proficiency in the investigative indicator supports success in the action indicator at the same class level. Same-rank direction is asserted on this investigate-then-apply substantive change, not on the shared chapter, domain or LC tokens alone. Evidence limitation: both endpoints carry upstream merge/code audit context and truncated source evidence (24 and 32 omitted source-evidence items), so the full source columns were not inspected; the shared chapter/table-row provenance is consistent with the judgment but the confidence is held moderate.

Shared LC tags (acceleration, motion) and adjacent source rows (42 vs 44) corroborate topical coherence but are not alone the basis. Direction is judged same-rank on this conceptual dependency; the alternative reading (mere parallel indicators under one chapter) keeps confidence moderate. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class IX (rank 0) Indicators in Chapter 15 'Improvement in food resources' under Content Domain 'Food', so the grain matches and direction must rest on substantive evidence rather than rank. C249 (second) asks learners to differentiate types of biological manures (compost, vermicompost, green manure) — a classification-level command of the manure types, including vermicompost. C271 (first) requires linking biotic and abiotic factors to the process of making vermicompost and to principles of biological control for environment conservation, and its LCs decompose exactly into those two integrative links under CLO115. Knowing what vermicompost is and how it differs from other biological manures plausibly supports success in the higher-order task of relating vermicompost production and biological control to biotic/abiotic interdependence, so the supported direction is C249 towards C271 (second_to_first). C141 ('Distinguishes between acquired and inherited traits') establishes the core conceptual discrimination between traits that are biologically inherited and those acquired during a lifetime. C163 ('Communicates awareness around perceptions of linking caste system to heredity and inheritance using validated videos, pictures, articles and posters') is an applied communication/advocacy outcome under CLO69/LO18 whose substance depends precisely on being able to judge what is and is not heritable; without the acquired-vs-inherited distinction a learner cannot meaningfully address the mistaken caste-heredity linkage. This is a substantive extension from conceptual discrimination to public communication of that concept, supporting a same-rank developmental direction from C141 to C163 rather than mere lexical overlap (the token/trigram overlap is low and mostly the shared 'heredity'/'inherit' stems plus 'and'). Endpoints sit under different parent CLOs in the DAG (CLO57 vs CLO69), so this is inferred coherence, not hierarchy. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and carries upstream merge/audit context, which limits certainty; confidence is moderate accordingly.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content Domain Specific Learning Outcomes of the same grain, both resolved at Class IX rank 0 under Chapter 13 'Why do we fall ill?' in 'World of living', so direction must rest on substantive same-rank evidence rather than shared parentage or page/trigram proximity. CLO97 (second) requires applying knowledge of infectious agents, transmission, symptoms and treatment to design appropriate preventive strategies for containment of disease in the neighbourhood/community (parent LO12, application of concepts in daily life). CLO100 (first) requires propagating awareness around communicable diseases and prevention strategies (parent LO18, communicating findings and conclusions effectively). The substantive disease-causation and prevention-strategy content that a learner must be able to design in CLO97 is precisely what is communicated and disseminated in CLO100, so proficiency in CLO97 supports success in CLO100; the reverse (awareness campaigning supporting design of containment strategies) is not supported by the supplied text. Evidence limitations: both endpoints carry upstream merge context and truncated source evidence (32 omitted source-evidence items each), so unseen source text could qualify this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X (rank 1) Indicators in the same Chapter 15 'Our Environment' under the Natural Resources Content Domain, but they sit on different parent paths: C238 under CLO104/LO1 (differentiating objects/phenomena, biodegradable vs non-biodegradable) and C246 under CLO105/LO3 (planning and conducting investigations about factors impacting ecosystems). The pair-specific substantive link is that the ability to classify wastes as biodegradable or non-biodegradable (C238) is the conceptual categorisation a learner applies when investigating how medical wastes are actually segregated and disposed at a health centre (C246); the investigative indicator extends the classification skill into a field inquiry about disposal practice, so proficiency in C238 supports success in C246. Same-rank direction is grounded in this classification-to-applied-investigation shift rather than on the shared Class, Chapter, LC 'waste' token overlap, or adjacent source pages, which alone would not establish a relation. Source evidence for both SFIs is truncated and both carry upstream merge/code audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded indicator texts and hierarchy shown.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators at the same resolved coordinate (Class IX, rank 0) within Chapter 6 – Tissues, so direction rests on substantive content rather than rank. C85 requires learners to locate regions of growth (apical, intercalary, lateral meristem) on the plant body — a locational/identification skill about where meristematic tissue sits. C88 requires observing and recording growth of onion root tips, relating that growth to the tissue type present there, and studying the effect of root tip removal; its LCs ('relates the growth of onion root tips with the type of tissues present there', 'studies the effect of root tip removal on growth') and its parent CLO33/LO3 (planning and conducting experiments to locate meristematic tissues) show an experimental, causal extension of the same meristem-growth content. Knowing where apical meristem is located directly supports interpreting root-tip growth data and the removal manipulation, so proficiency in C85 supports success in C88 rather than the reverse. Shared ancestry, page proximity, and the generic 'growth'/stopword token overlap were treated as nomination signal only; the judgment rests on the pair-specific content relationship. Endpoint source evidence is truncated, so the full source rows were not inspectable.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain SFIs at the same canonical coordinate (Class X, rank 1) within Chapter 15 – Our Environment under Content Domain 'Natural Resources', but they sit under different parents (CLO104 differentiation of environment-related objects/phenomena vs CLO110 calculation of energy at trophic levels, LO1 vs LO8). Same-rank direction is justified by substantive pair-specific content, not by the shared Chapter/Class or the 'food chain' token overlap alone: C241 establishes the structural distinction between a food chain and a food web (LC tags: ecosystem, food chain, food web), which is the conceptual model of linear trophic sequences that C258's quantitative work presupposes, since C258 requires locating trophic levels within a food chain and computing energy available at each from given data (LC tags: calculation, energy, food chain, trophic levels). Proficiency in identifying and distinguishing food chains therefore supports success in the more complex quantitative trophic-energy calculation, making first_to_second the supported developmental direction. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and several ancestors carry merge/audit context (LO1, LO8, Content Domain and Chapter organizers merged), so the judgment rests on the visible indicator text, coordinates, and LCs.

judgment.rationale: Both are Indicator-grain statements at the same resolved coordinate (Class X, rank 1) within Chapter 15 'Our Environment' under Content Domain 'Natural Resources', so the judgment rests on substantive same-rank evidence rather than rank order. C254 ('Explains the flow of energy across trophic levels') establishes the explanatory model of trophic-level energy transfer; C259 asks students to apply interdependence of organisms and environmental factors to predict consequences, with its own source excerpt naming 'Effect of removal and addition of trophic level in an ecosystem' as the exemplar situation. Understanding how energy moves across trophic levels is the specific conceptual basis that makes predicting the consequences of altering a trophic level tractable, a shift from explanation to applied prediction that supports a developmental direction from C254 to C259. The pair also shares the LC tag 'ecosystem', but that overlap is corroborative only; the pair-specific trophic-level content link carries the judgment. Both endpoints' bounded source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment is limited to the trustworthy statement text and hierarchy supplied; parent paths differ (CLO107/LO5 versus CLO111/LO11) and were read as separate DAG paths, not a single sequence.
